nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-01.title: Find both ends
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-01.body:
The smallest supaprime is $2\cdot3=6$. Checking down from $49$: $49=7^2$ (primes not distinct), $48=2^4\cdot3$ and $47$ (prime) fail, while $46=2\cdot23$ works. The difference is $46-6=40$.

**Answer: 40**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-02.title: Deficit from 99999
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-02.body:
Four digits sum to at most $36<43$, so $k=5$ (e.g. $79999$). A $5$-digit number with digit sum $43$ falls short of $99999$ (sum $45$) by $2$. Either one digit is $7$ ($5$ ways) or two digits are $8$ ($\binom52=10$ ways). The leading digit is never $0$, so there are $15$ such numbers.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-02.title: Stars and bars
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-02.body:
Let $e_i=9-d_i\ge0$ be the deficits; we need $e_1+\dots+e_5=2$, which has $\binom{6}{4}=15$ solutions, all with every digit at least $7$.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-03.title: Right angles and best pairing
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-03.body:
A parallelogram with sides $a,b$ and angle $\theta$ has area $ab\sin\theta\le ab$, with equality for a rectangle. So we maximize $ab+cd$ over the three ways to pair the numbers:
- $20\cdot23+40\cdot46=460+1840=2300$,
- $20\cdot40+23\cdot46=800+1058=1858$,
- $20\cdot46+23\cdot40=920+920=1840$.

The maximum is $2300$.

**Answer: 2300**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-04.title: Common denominator
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-04.body:
$\left|\frac ab-\frac cd\right|=\frac{|ad-bc|}{bd}$. The numerator is a positive integer, so it is at least $1$. If $b=d$, the value is at least $\frac1{10}$; if $b\ne d$, then $bd\le 9\cdot10=90$, so the value is at least $\frac1{90}$. This is achieved by $\frac19-\frac1{10}=\frac1{90}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{90}$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-05.title: Count sequences
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-05.body:
On day 1 he has $5$ choices; on each later day $4$ choices (any borough but the current one). So there are $5\cdot4^4=1280$ equally likely five-day trips. Visiting all five boroughs in five days means visiting them in some order with no repeats, which can happen in $5!=120$ ways. The probability is $\frac{120}{1280}=\frac3{32}$.

**Answer: $\frac3{32}$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-05.title: Day by day
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-05.body:
Day 1 is always new. On day 2 all $4$ choices are new, since the only visited borough is the current one. On day 3, of the $4$ choices, $3$ are new; on day 4, $2$ of $4$; on day 5, $1$ of $4$. The probability is $1\cdot1\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac24\cdot\frac14=\frac3{32}$.

**Answer: $\frac3{32}$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-06.title: A right angle at A
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-06.body:
In right triangle $AEB$, the acute angles $\angle EAB$ and $\angle ABE$ are equal, so both are $45^\circ$ and $AB=4\sqrt2$. Since $AD$ bisects $\angle A$, $\angle BAC=2\cdot45^\circ=90^\circ$. Then $AC=\sqrt{BC^2-AB^2}=\sqrt{81-32}=7$, and the area is $\frac12\cdot4\sqrt2\cdot7=14\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $14\sqrt2$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-07.title: Check the triangle inequality
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-07.body:
There are $\binom43=4$ choices of three sticks. $2,5,7$ fails since $2+5=7$. The others work: $2+5>6$, $2+6>7$, $5+6>7$. So $3$ triangles.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-08.title: Squarefree numbers divide
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-08.body:
Each $a_k=3\cdot5\cdot7\cdots p_k$ contains each odd prime at most once. An odd number divides some $a_k$ exactly when it has no repeated prime factor (then take $k$ large enough to include all its primes). Checking: $91=7\cdot13$, $93=3\cdot31$, $95=5\cdot19$, $97$ prime are all squarefree, but $99=3^2\cdot11$ is not.

**Answer: 99**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-09.title: Jelly = bread minus sandwiches
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-09.body:
A sandwich with $b$ slices uses $b-1$ scoops. With $s$ sandwiches using all $13$ slices, Jacob uses $13-s$ scoops. Each sandwich needs at least $2$ slices, so $1\le s\le 6$, and every such $s$ is possible (e.g. $s-1$ two-slice sandwiches and one with the rest). So $m\in\{7,8,\dots,12\}$ with sum $57$.

**Answer: 57**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-11.title: Powers of 9
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-11.body:
$20^2-1=399$ ends in $9$, and powers of a number ending in $9$ end in $9,1,9,1,\dots$ (odd exponent gives $9$, even gives $1$). The exponent $23^2-1=528$ is even, so the last digit is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-12.title: Solve the floor equation
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-12.body:
$\lfloor nx\rfloor=n+10$ means $n+10\le nx<n+11$, i.e. $x\in\left[\frac{n+10}n,\frac{n+11}n\right)$. Then $a+b=\frac{2n+21}n=2+\frac{21}n$, an integer exactly when $n\mid 21$: $n=1,3,7,21$, with sum $32$.

**Answer: 32**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-13.title: Shift the decimal
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-13.body:
$\frac13=0.333\ldots$, and dividing by $1000$ moves the decimal point three places: $\frac1{3000}=0.000333\ldots$. There are $3$ zeros before the first $3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-14.title: Undo one swap
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-14.body:
The good orders are exactly those obtained from NYCIML by swapping one pair of tiles, since that swap can be undone. There are $\binom62=15$ pairs, giving $15$ different orders (NYCIML itself is not one: any swap would change it). The probability is $\frac{15}{6!}=\frac{15}{720}=\frac1{48}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{48}$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-15.title: Find $OT$ and use $\sin 60^\circ$
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-15.body:
$OPQ$ is an equilateral triangle and $PQRS$ a unit square. Line $OP$ makes a $60^\circ$ angle with $PQ$, so in right triangle $PST$ (right angle at $S$, $PS=1$, $\angle TPS=30^\circ$) we get $PT=\frac{PS}{\cos30^\circ}=\frac2{\sqrt3}=\frac{2\sqrt3}3$. Thus $OT=1+\frac{2\sqrt3}3$, and since $\angle QOT=60^\circ$ and $OQ=1$,
$$[OQT]=\frac12\cdot OT\cdot OQ\cdot\sin60^\circ=\frac12\left(1+\frac{2\sqrt3}3\right)\frac{\sqrt3}2=\frac{\sqrt3}4+\frac12.$$

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt3}4+\frac12$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-15.title: Coordinates
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-15.body:
Put $P=(0,0)$, $Q=(1,0)$, $O=\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)$, $S=(0,-1)$, $R=(1,-1)$. Line $OP$ is $y=\sqrt3x$, meeting $y=-1$ at $T=\left(-\frac1{\sqrt3},-1\right)$. By the shoelace formula,
$$[OQT]=\frac12\left|\left(\tfrac12\right)(0+1)+1\left(-1-\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)-\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\left(\tfrac{\sqrt3}2-0\right)\right|=\frac12\left|-1-\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\right|=\frac12+\frac{\sqrt3}4.$$

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt3}4+\frac12$**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-16.title: Reduce to a totient
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-16.body:
Write $a=17x$, $b=17y$ with $\gcd(x,y)=1$. Then $x+y=\frac{2023}{17}=119$, and $\gcd(x,119-x)=\gcd(x,119)$. So we need $1\le x\le118$ with $\gcd(x,119)=1$. Since $119=7\cdot17$, the count is $\varphi(119)=6\cdot16=96$.

**Answer: 96**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-16.title: Inclusion–exclusion
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-16.body:
Multiples of $17$ for $a$ give $118$ pairs. Since $\gcd(a,b)$ divides $2023=7\cdot17^2$, the gcd is too big exactly when $7\cdot17=119\mid a$ ($16$ pairs) or $17^2=289\mid a$ ($6$ pairs), and no $a<2023$ is divisible by both. So $118-16-6=96$.

**Answer: 96**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-17.title: Add the ranges
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-17.body:
$6.5\le a<7.5$ and $7.5\le b<8.5$, so $14\le a+b<16$, and every value in that range occurs. Rounding gives $14$ (for $a+b<14.5$), $15$, or $16$ (for $a+b\ge15.5$). The sum is $14+15+16=45$.

**Answer: 45**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-18.title: Similar right triangles
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-18.body:
Let $F$ be the point where $\omega$ touches $CD$. Then $OF=3$ and $OF\perp CD$, so $CF=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4$. Since $OE\perp AD$ and $E,O,C$ are collinear, $CE\perp AD$ with $CE=8$. Right triangles $CFO$ and $CED$ share the angle at $C$, so $\frac{CD}{CE}=\frac{CO}{CF}$, giving $CD=8\cdot\frac54=10$. The circle is tangent to the parallel lines $AB$ and $CD$, so the distance between them is the diameter $6$. The area is $CD\cdot6=60$.

**Answer: 60**

nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-18.title: Two expressions for the area
nyciml-2023-24-fall-sophfrosh-18.body:
With $CD=10$ as above, the area is $AB\cdot 6=60$. As a check, using base $AD$ with height $CE=8$ gives $AD=\frac{60}8=7.5<10=AB$, consistent with the given $AD<AB$.

**Answer: 60**
